rationale: This Shootout 'lists' benchmark is tiny (13 functions, ~1.7 KB text) but contains hot loops (list traversal/copy in test_lists, hash lookups, matrix/ary3 kernels), so cheap, low-risk transformations dominate: SUB gets the highest weights (near-zero runtime/size cost, strong diversity for such small basic blocks), with SPLIT as an almost-free complement. FLA and BCF are favored moderately on security because test_lists (899 bytes) and the loop kernels are the real reverse-engineering targets, but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are held mid-range so the selector applies them selectively to the largest/hottest functions rather than blanket coverage, keeping the shootout-style runtime acceptable. IBR and IGV are enabled with moderate security/diversity weights and restrained cost weights to disrupt control-flow recovery without bloating a binary that is already minuscule. ICALL is kept at the lowest tier: this C code has few indirect-call sites to protect, its dispatch overhead lands directly in the hot loops, and its higher CorrectnessRisk weight guards against miscompilation of function-pointer-heavy code in simple_hash.h/methcall.c.
